title: Shama Hyder Named to 2026 TIME100 Creators List for AI and Business Strategy Influence
excerpt: The Indian American entrepreneur, who founded Zen Media at 22 and now leads executive advisory Roster & Co., was recognized for her work at the intersection of technology and human behavior.
body:
• Business strategist Shama Hyder has been named to the 2026 TIME100 Creators list, which recognizes the world's most influential digital voices.
  • Hyder founded Zen Media at 22, grew it into a globally recognized B2B agency serving Fortune 500 clients, and sold it after 17 years.
  • The recognition follows five Indian Americans making the inaugural TIME100 Creators list in 2025, continuing a pattern of strong diaspora representation across TIME's franchise lists.

Shama Hyder, a business strategist and AI authority, has been named to the 2026 TIME100 Creators list, which recognizes 100 of the world's most influential digital voices. The full list appears in the July 27, 2026 issue of TIME magazine.

Hyder was recognized for her work at the intersection of emerging technology and human behavior — a niche she has carved over nearly two decades as an entrepreneur, author, and keynote speaker.

From Zen Media to Roster & Co.

Hyder founded Zen Media at 22 as one of the earliest remote-first companies in the United States. She grew it into a globally recognized B2B marketing and PR agency serving Fortune 500 clients before selling it 17 years later.

Today, she is co-founder and CEO of Roster & Co., an executive advisory firm she launched with Nick Tran, TikTok's former Global Head of Marketing. The firm helps leaders turn AI capabilities into business growth through its Rewired programs, which teach AI fluency to executives and teams.

"I built my audience the long way, alongside a company I ran for 17 years. This recognition reflects a broader shift in what audiences value: perspective, experience, and the ability to translate change into action."

— Shama Hyder, CEO of Roster & Co.

The Six Signals Framework

Hyder created the Six Signals framework, a methodology designed to help leaders identify change earlier, interpret what matters, and act with strategic urgency. She also publishes the Hyder Index, a monthly measure of the Change-Response Gap — the disconnect between how quickly technology changes and how quickly organizations respond — across 15 industries.

She currently serves as Applied AI Evangelist for Wispr Flow and as a Professor of Practice at Link School of Business, where she teaches a course called Communication in the Age of AI. She has delivered more than 500 keynotes across 26 countries.

Two forthcoming books round out her profile: Miami Masala from Regalo Press and Six Signals from Simon & Schuster.

Indian Americans and the TIME100 Franchise

Hyder's recognition is part of a broader pattern of Indian American representation across TIME's expanding franchise of lists. The inaugural TIME100 Creators list in 2025 featured five Indian Americans: entrepreneur Dhar Mann, YouTubers Prajakta Koli, Michelle Khare, and Samir Chaudry, and podcaster Jay Shetty.

Separately, the 2026 TIME100 main list included five Indian Americans — Google CEO Sundar Pichai, YouTube CEO Neal Mohan, chef Vikas Khanna, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and University of Pennsylvania cardiologist Kiran Musunuru. The 2026 TIME100 Health list featured five more, and the TIME100 Philanthropy list included three.

The cumulative presence underscores the community's expanding influence across technology, media, business, science, and public life.

What's Next

The TIME100 Creators list is available online at ti.me/100creators and in the print edition dated July 27. Hyder's full profile can be found on TIME's website. As the creator economy continues to mature beyond entertainment into business strategy and AI, Hyder's inclusion signals recognition of a different kind of digital influence — one rooted in expertise rather than follower counts.
